notes.s: The love was real to him, and keeping it meant deleting himself.
notes.t: Lead single of Love Yourself 轉 Tear, May 2018, the album that gave BTS their first number one on the Billboard 200. 轉 is the turn in a four-part Korean narrative structure, and this is where the certainty of DNA breaks: the narrator worked out who the other person wanted and became that, and now there is nobody left behind the performance. The emo-trap production and the collapsing set in the video were a deliberate break from the brightness of the previous era. It was the first BTS single where the hit chorus is an admission of failure, and ARMY reads it as a song about any relationship that runs on performance, including the one with an audience.
k: -(으)ㄴ/는 척하다 is to put on an act of being something. Attach it to an adjective stem for a false front: 모르는 척 pretending not to know, 괜찮은 척 pretending to be fine. The song's whole first verse is built on it, which is why the chorus can call the love fake without ever calling the feeling fake.

-길 is the contraction of -기를, a verb turned into a noun plus the object marker, with the wishing verb 바라다 deleted off the end. What is left is a wish with no one to wish it to, which reads like prayer. Full form 완벽하기를 바라다, I hope it is perfect.

꽃을 피우다 is the set idiom for bringing something to bloom or making an effort pay off, and 키우다 is to raise or grow. The line pairs them against each other: he kept tending the one thing that by definition was never going to open. Not a translation problem, a contradiction built on purpose.

A slangy self-cancelling frame, X-긴 뭐가 X, roughly what do you mean it isn't, of course it is. The next line runs the same shape on love itself, 사랑은 뭐가 사랑. Worth knowing because the words look like a plain question and the meaning is sarcastic rejection.

vocab.en: to pretend, to act as if

vocab.note: 약 weak plus 점 point. The opposite, a strong point, is 장점
숨다 is to hide yourself, 숨기다 is to hide a thing. The -기- in the middle is the causative

vocab.en: to come true, to be realized
vocab.note: Passive of 이루다, to achieve. Used of dreams and wishes
Covers children, pets, plants and abilities with no change of word
Both the one you have asleep and the one you chase, as in English
-어버리다 adds the sense that it is gone for good, often with regret or relief

vocab.en: to blab, to run one's mouth
vocab.note: Openly rude. Never use it about an elder's speech
Drops into a question to add exasperation. A separate noun 대체 means substitute
The literary short form. Spoken Korean says 거짓말
빚다 is for shaping clay or kneading rice cake dough. Applying it to lies is the striking part of the line
As an ending on another verb it means to do something off completely, as in 잊어버리다
낯 is the face. The opposite is 낯익다, to look familiar
In lyrics almost always figurative, blinded by love or greed
Irregular, 몰라 and 몰랐어. It is its own verb, not a negated 알다
